questions.question: A businessman’s earnings increase by 25% in one year but decreases by 4% in the next. Going by this pattern, after 5 years, his earning would be Rs. 72000. What is his present earning?
questions.questionHtml: A businessman’s earnings increase by 25% in one year but decreases by 4% in the next. Going by this pattern, after 5 years, his earning would be Rs. 72000. What is his present earning?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Successive Multiplier for 2 years (Cycle): (1 + 25/100) × (1 − 4/100) = 5/4 × 24/25 = 6/5 = 1.2

Total time = 5 years = 2 full cycles (4 years) + Year 5 (+25%)

Total Multiplier = 1.2 × 1.2 × 1.25 = 1.44 × 1.25 = 1.8

Present Earning = 72000 ÷ 1.8 = 40000

∴ The correct answer is ₹40,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Earnings after 5 years = ₹72,000

Pattern: Year 1, 3, 5 (+25%) and Year 2, 4 (−4%)

Formula Used:

Final Value = Present Earning × (1 + r1/100) × (1 − r2/100) × ...

Calculations:

⇒ Let Present Earning be P.

⇒ 72000 = P × (125/100) × (96/100) × (125/100) × (96/100) × (125/100)

⇒ 72000 = P × (5/4) × (24/25) × (5/4) × (24/25) × (5/4)

⇒ 72000 = P × (5/4 × 24/25) × (5/4 × 24/25) × 5/4

⇒ 72000 = P × (6/5) × (6/5) × 5/4

⇒ 72000 = P × (36/25) × 5/4

⇒ 72000 = P × (9/5)

⇒ P = (72000 × 5) ÷ 9

⇒ P = 8000 × 5

⇒ P = 40000

∴ The correct answer is ₹40,000.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes by a% and then b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: [a + b + (a × b)/100]%.

Fraction Multiplier Method

Convert percentage increase/decrease into fractions (e.g., +25% = 5/4, −4% = 24/25) and multiply them sequentially for the total factor.

Compounded Growth

Earning patterns like these follow the principle of Compound Interest where the base changes after every increment or decrement.

questions.question: In an examination 73% of the candidates passed in quantitative aptitude test, 70% passed in General awareness and 64% passed in both. If 6300 failed in both subjects the total number of examinees were
questions.questionHtml: In an examination 73% of the candidates passed in quantitative aptitude test, 70% passed in General awareness and 64% passed in both. If 6300 failed in both subjects the total number of examinees were
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total % passed in at least one subject = %Passed(QA) + %Passed(GA) − %Passed(Both)

Total Passed % = 73% + 70% − 64% = 79%

Total Failed % = 100% − 79% = 21%

Since 21% of total students = 6300

Total examinees = (6300 ÷ 21) × 100 = 30000

∴ The correct answer is 30000 examinees.

Alternate Method

Given:

Candidates passed in QA = 73%

Candidates passed in GA = 70%

Candidates passed in both = 64%

Number of candidates failed in both = 6300

Calculations:

⇒ Candidates passed in QA only = 73% − 64% = 9%

⇒ Candidates passed in GA only = 70% − 64% = 6%

⇒ Total candidates who passed in at least one subject = (QA only) + (GA only) + (Both)

⇒ Total Passed % = 9% + 6% + 64% = 79%

⇒ Candidates who failed in both subjects = 100% − 79% = 21%

⇒ Let total number of examinees be X.

⇒ 21% of X = 6300

⇒ (21 ÷ 100) × X = 6300

⇒ X = (6300 × 100) ÷ 21

⇒ X = 300 × 100

⇒ X = 30000

∴ The correct answer is 30000 examinees.

Additional Information

Inclusion-Exclusion Principle (2 Sets)

For two sets A and B, n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B). This represents the union of two groups.

Venn Diagram for Failed Candidates

Total Failed = 100 − (Passed in at least one). Alternatively, you can solve using fail percentages directly: %Fail(Both) = 100 − [%Pass(A) + %Pass(B) − %Pass(A ∩ B)].

Case of 3 Sets

For three sets A, B, and C: n(A ∪ B ∪ C) = n(A) + n(B) + n(C) − n(A ∩ B) − n(B ∩ C) − n(A ∩ C) + n(A ∩ B ∩ C).

questions.question: A man spends 75% of his income. His income increases by 20% and his expenditure also increases by 10%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
questions.questionHtml: A man spends 75% of his income. His income increases by 20% and his expenditure also increases by 10%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let initial Income = 100, then Expenditure = 75 and Savings = 25.

Ratio of Expenditure : Savings = 75 : 25 = 3 : 1.

Using the weighted average method for Net Income Increase:

(3 × 10%) + (1 × x%) = 4 × 20%

30 + x = 80 ⇒ x = 50%

∴ The correct answer is 50%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expenditure = 75% of Income

Income Increase = 20%

Expenditure Increase = 10%

Formula used: Savings = Income − Expenditure

⇒ Let initial Income = ₹100

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 75% of 100 = ₹75

⇒ Initial Savings = 100 − 75 = ₹25

⇒ New Income = 100 + (20% of 100) = ₹120

⇒ New Expenditure = 75 + (10% of 75) = 75 + 7.5 = ₹82.5

⇒ New Savings = 120 − 82.5 = ₹37.5

⇒ Increase in Savings = 37.5 − 25 = ₹12.5

⇒ Percentage increase in savings = (12.5 ÷ 25) × 100 = 50%

∴ The correct answer is 50%.

Additional Information

Income Relation

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any change in two variables directly impacts the third.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Base Change Rule

When calculating percentage increase/decrease, always ensure the denominator is the original (initial) value of that specific component.

questions.question: On a river, Q is the mid-point between two points P and R on the same bank of the river. A boat can go from P to Q and back in 12 hours, and from P to R in 16 hours 40 min. How long would it take to go from R to P?
questions.questionHtml: On a river, Q is the mid-point between two points P and R on the same bank of the river. A boat can go from P to Q and back in 12 hours, and from P to R in 16 hours 40 min. How long would it take to go from R to P?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Q is the midpoint ⇒ Round trip time for PR is exactly twice the round trip time for PQ.

Total time for (P → R) + (R → P) = 2 × 12 hours = 24 hours.

Given: Time taken for P → R = 16 hours 40 minutes.

Time for R → P = Total round trip time − Time for P → R.

Time for R → P = 24 hr − 16 hr 40 min = 7 hr 20 min = 71/3 hr.

∴ The correct answer is 71/3 hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time (P → Q + Q → P) = 12 hr

Time (P → R) = 16 hr 40 min = 162/3 hr

Q is the midpoint of PR ⇒ PQ = QR = 1/2 PR

Since the speed is constant for the same direction:

⇒ Time (P → Q) = 1/2 × Time (P → R)

⇒ Time (P → Q) = 1/2 × 16 hr 40 min = 8 hr 20 min

⇒ From (P → Q + Q → P) = 12 hr:

⇒ Time (Q → P) = 12 hr − 8 hr 20 min = 3 hr 40 min

⇒ Since Q is the midpoint, Time (R → P) = 2 × Time (Q → P)

⇒ Time (R → P) = 2 × 3 hr 40 min = 6 hr 80 min

⇒ Time (R → P) = 7 hr 20 min = 720/60 hr = 71/3 hr

∴ The correct answer is 71/3 hr.

Additional Information

Upstream and Downstream Speed

Downstream speed (a) = u + v and Upstream speed (b) = u − v, where u is boat speed in still water and v is stream speed.

Midpoint Time Relation

For a constant speed, the time taken to travel half the distance is exactly half of the total time: thalf = ttotal ÷ 2.

Average Speed Formula

For a round trip with speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

questions.question: A car can finish a certain journey in 10 hours at a speed of 42 kmph. In order to cover the same distance in 7 hours, the speed of the car (km/h) must be increased by:
questions.questionHtml: A car can finish a certain journey in 10 hours at a speed of 42 kmph. In order to cover the same distance in 7 hours, the speed of the car (km/h) must be increased by:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time.

Ratio of Time (T1 : T2) = 10 : 7

Ratio of Speed (S1 : S2) = 7 : 10

Given S1 = 42 kmph ⇒ 7 units = 42 kmph ⇒ 1 unit = 6 kmph

Increase in speed = 10 − 7 = 3 units = 3 × 6 = 18 kmph

∴ The correct answer is 18 kmph.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Speed (S1) = 42 kmph

Initial Time (T1) = 10 hours

New Time (T2) = 7 hours

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Total Distance = S1 × T1

⇒ Total Distance = 42 × 10 = 420 km

⇒ New Speed (S2) = Total Distance ÷ T2

⇒ S2 = 420 ÷ 7 = 60 kmph

⇒ Increase in speed = S2 − S1

⇒ Increase = 60 − 42 = 18 kmph

∴ The correct answer is 18 kmph.

Additional Information

Constant Distance Rule

If distance is constant, S1 × T1 = S2 × T2. This is used to find any one missing variable when the other three are known.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed = S1 − S2. For opposite directions, relative speed = S1 + S2.

Unit Conversion

To convert kmph to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A man travels 450 km to his home partly by train and partly by car. He takes 8 hrs 40 mins if he travels 240 km by train and rest by car. He takes 20 mins more if he travels 180 km by train and the rest by car. The speed of the car in km/hr is
questions.questionHtml: A man travels 450 km to his home partly by train and partly by car. He takes 8 hrs 40 mins if he travels 240 km by train and rest by car. He takes 20 mins more if he travels 180 km by train and the rest by car. The speed of the car in km/hr is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Change in mode: 60 km less by train and 60 km more by car increases time by 20 mins.

To eliminate the train journey entirely, we shift the remaining 240 km from train to car.

Additional time for 240 km shift = (240 ÷ 60) × 20 mins = 80 mins.

Total time if the entire 450 km is covered by car = 8 hr 40 min + 80 min = 10 hr.

Speed of car = Total distance ÷ Total time = 450 ÷ 10 = 45 km/hr.

∴ The correct answer is 45 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given: Total Distance = 450 km.

Case 1: Train = 240 km, Car = 210 km, Time = 8 hr 40 min = 26/3 hrs.

Case 2: Train = 180 km, Car = 270 km, Time = 9 hr.

Let speed of train be T and car be C.

⇒ 240/T + 210/C = 26/3 — (Eq 1)

⇒ 180/T + 270/C = 9 — (Eq 2)

Multiply Eq 1 by 3 and Eq 2 by 4 to eliminate T:

⇒ 720/T + 630/C = 26

⇒ 720/T + 1080/C = 36

Subtracting the two equations:

⇒ (1080 − 630) / C = 36 − 26

⇒ 450/C = 10

⇒ C = 45 km/hr.

∴ The correct answer is 45 km/hr.

Additional Information

Average Speed

Average speed is the ratio of total distance covered to the total time taken. Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Speed Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = |u − v|. If they move in opposite directions, relative speed = u + v.

questions.question: A train 'B' speeding with 100 kmph crosses another train C, running in the same direction, in 2 mins. If the length of the train B and C be 150m and 250m respectively, what is the speed of the train C (in kmph)?
questions.questionHtml: A train 'B' speeding with 100 kmph crosses another train C, running in the same direction, in 2 mins. If the length of the train B and C be 150m and 250m respectively, what is the speed of the train C (in kmph)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance to cover = Sum of lengths = 150 + 250 = 400 m = 0.4 km.

Time taken = 2 minutes = 2/60 = 1/30 hours.

Relative speed in same direction = Distance ÷ Time = 0.4 ÷ (1/30) = 12 kmph.

Relative speed = Faster speed − Slower speed ⇒ 12 = 100 − Speed of Train C.

Speed of Train C = 100 − 12 = 88 kmph.

∴ The correct answer is 88 kmph.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of Train B (VB) = 100 kmph

Length of Train B (LB) = 150 m

Length of Train C (LC) = 250 m

Time (t) = 2 minutes = 120 seconds

Formula Used:

Relative Speed (Same direction) = (L1 + L2) ÷ Time

To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.

Calculations:

⇒ Total distance to be covered = 150 + 250 = 400 m

⇒ Total time taken = 120 seconds

⇒ Relative speed (in m/s) = 400 ÷ 120 = 10/3 m/s

⇒ Relative speed (in kmph) = (10/3) × (18/5)

⇒ Relative speed = 2 × 6 = 12 kmph

⇒ Since both trains move in the same direction: VB − VC = 12

⇒ 100 − VC = 12

⇒ VC = 100 − 12 = 88 kmph

∴ The correct answer is 88 kmph.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S1 − S2|. When they move in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S1 + S2.

Crossing Rule

Whether moving in same or opposite directions, the distance covered while crossing each other is always the sum of their lengths (L1 + L2).

Unit Conversion

1 kmph = 5/18 m/s and 1 m/s = 18/5 kmph.

questions.question: The compound interest on Rs. 30,000 at 7% per annum for n years is Rs. 4347. The value of n is
questions.questionHtml: The compound interest on Rs. 30,000 at 7% per annum for n years is Rs. 4347. The value of n is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Compound Interest percentage = (4347 ÷ 30000) × 100 = 14.49%.

Given annual rate (R) = 7%.

Effective interest for 2 years = R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100.

Effective rate = 7 + 7 + (49 ÷ 100) = 14.49%.

Since the calculated interest percentage matches the required effective rate, n = 2.

∴ The correct answer is 2 years.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = ₹30,000, Rate (R) = 7% p.a., Compound Interest (CI) = ₹4,347.

Formula used: Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)n, where A = P + CI.

⇒ Amount (A) = 30000 + 4347 = ₹34,347

⇒ 34347 = 30000(1 + 7/100)n

⇒ 34347 ÷ 30000 = (107/100)n

⇒ 11449 ÷ 10000 = (1.07)n

⇒ (107 ÷ 100)2 = (1.07)n

⇒ (1.07)2 = (1.07)n

⇒ n = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2 years.

Additional Information

Effective Interest Rate

For a rate R, the effective compound interest rate for 2 years is calculated as R + R + (R2 ÷ 100)%.

CI vs SI Difference

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is given by P × (R ÷ 100)2.

Amount in Compound Interest

The total amount A after n years is A = P(1 + r/100)n, where compounding is done annually.

questions.question: If A borrowed Rs. P at x% and B borrowed Rs. Q(>P) at y% per annum at simple interest at the same time, then the amount of their debts will be equal after
questions.questionHtml: If A borrowed Rs. P at x% and B borrowed Rs. Q(>P) at y% per annum at simple interest at the same time, then the amount of their debts will be equal after
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Equate the final amount for both persons A and B.

Amount = Principal + (Principal × Rate × Time) ÷ 100

P + (P × x × t) ÷ 100 = Q + (Q × y × t) ÷ 100

(Pxt − Qyt) ÷ 100 = Q − P

t (Px − Qy) = 100(Q − P)

∴ The correct answer is 100 ((Q − P) ÷ (Px − Qy)) years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal for A = ₹ P, Rate for A = x% per annum

Principal for B = ₹ Q, Rate for B = y% per annum

Let the time after which their debts become equal be 't' years.

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

Calculations:

⇒ Amount for A = P + (P × x × t) ÷ 100

⇒ Amount for B = Q + (Q × y × t) ÷ 100

According to the question, these amounts are equal:

⇒ P + (Pxt ÷ 100) = Q + (Qyt ÷ 100)

⇒ (Pxt ÷ 100) − (Qyt ÷ 100) = Q − P

⇒ (t ÷ 100) × (Px − Qy) = Q − P

⇒ t × (Px − Qy) = 100 × (Q − P)

⇒ t = 100 × (Q − P) ÷ (Px − Qy)

∴ The correct answer is 100 ((Q − P) ÷ (Px − Qy)) years.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate of Interest, and T is Time in years.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total debt or maturity value is A = P + SI = P(1 + RT ÷ 100).

Rate and Time Units

Ensure the Rate (R) is per annum and Time (T) is in years. If time is in months, divide by 12; if in days, divide by 365.

questions.question: A man invested a sum of money at compound interest. It amounted to Rs. 2420 in 2 years and to Rs. 2662 in 3 years. Find the sum
questions.questionHtml: A man invested a sum of money at compound interest. It amounted to Rs. 2420 in 2 years and to Rs. 2662 in 3 years. Find the sum
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Multiplying factor for 1 year = Amount after 3 years ÷ Amount after 2 years

Factor = 2662 ÷ 2420 = 1.1 = 11/10

We know, Amount after 2 years = Principal × (Multiplying factor)2

2420 = P × (11/10)2

P = 2420 × (100 / 121) = 2000

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 2 years (A2) = Rs. 2420

Amount after 3 years (A3) = Rs. 2662

Formula Used:

Amount = P(1 + R/100)T

Calculations:

⇒ In compound interest, the amount of the previous year acts as the principal for the next year.

⇒ Interest for the 3rd year = A3 − A2

⇒ Interest = 2662 − 2420 = Rs. 242

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (Interest / Principal for 3rd year) × 100

⇒ R = (242 / 2420) × 100 = 10%

⇒ Now, substitute the rate into the formula for the amount after 2 years:

⇒ 2420 = P(1 + 10/100)2

⇒ 2420 = P(11/10)2

⇒ 2420 = P × (121 / 100)

⇒ P = (2420 × 100) / 121

⇒ P = 20 × 100 = 2000

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2000.

Additional Information

Compound Interest Successive Method

Compound Interest works exactly like successive percentage increments. For a 10% rate, the value increases by 10% each year (Multiplier = 1.1).

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective interest rate for 2 years at R% p.a. is given by the formula (2R + R2/100)%. For R = 10%, the 2-year CI is 21%.

Difference between SI and CI

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years is calculated using the formula: Difference = P × (R/100)2.

questions.question: If a sum of money becomes 4000 in 2 yrs and 5500 in 4 yrs 6 months at the same rate of simple interest per annum. Then the rate of simple interest is
questions.questionHtml: If a sum of money becomes 4000 in 2 yrs and 5500 in 4 yrs 6 months at the same rate of simple interest per annum. Then the rate of simple interest is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for (4.5 − 2) = 2.5 years = 5500 − 4000 = ₹1500.

Simple Interest for 1 year = 1500 ÷ 2.5 = ₹600.

Simple Interest for 2 years = 600 × 2 = ₹1200.

Principal (P) = 4000 − 1200 = ₹2800.

Rate (R) = (600 ÷ 2800) × 100 = 150 ÷ 7 = 213/7%.

∴ The correct answer is 213/7%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 2 years (A1) = ₹4000

Amount after 4 years 6 months (A2) = ₹5500

Time period 1 (T1) = 2 years

Time period 2 (T2) = 4.5 years

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

Calculations:

⇒ SI for (4.5 − 2) years = 5500 − 4000

⇒ SI for 2.5 years = ₹1500

⇒ SI for 1 year = 1500 ÷ 2.5 = ₹600

⇒ SI for 2 years = 600 × 2 = ₹1200

⇒ Principal (P) = A1 − SI for 2 years

⇒ P = 4000 − 1200 = ₹2800

⇒ Rate (R) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ P

⇒ R = (600 × 100) ÷ 2800

⇒ R = 600 ÷ 28 = 150 ÷ 7

⇒ R = 213/7%

∴ The correct answer is 213/7%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Property

In Simple Interest, the interest earned remains constant for every year as it is always calculated on the original Principal amount.

Rate of Interest Formula

Rate % = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T). It represents the interest earned on ₹100 for a period of one year.

Principal from Amount

Principal (P) = Amount (A) − Simple Interest (SI). For multiple periods, P = A1 − SI1 = A2 − SI2.

questions.question: A hollow cylindrical tube 20 cm long is made of iron and its external and internal diameters are 8 cm and 6 cm respectively. The volume (in cubic cm) of iron used in making the tube is (Take n = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: A hollow cylindrical tube 20 cm long is made of iron and its external and internal diameters are 8 cm and 6 cm respectively. The volume (in cubic cm) of iron used in making the tube is (Take n = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of iron = π × (R2 − r2) × h

Given: R = 4 cm (external), r = 3 cm (internal), h = 20 cm

Volume = (22/7) × (42 − 32) × 20

Volume = (22/7) × 7 × 20 = 440 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 440 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of the tube (h) = 20 cm

External diameter = 8 cm ⇒ External radius (R) = 8/2 = 4 cm

Internal diameter = 6 cm ⇒ Internal radius (r) = 6/2 = 3 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of hollow cylinder = πh(R2 − r2)

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of iron = (22/7) × 20 × (42 − 32)

⇒ Volume of iron = (22/7) × 20 × (16 − 9)

⇒ Volume of iron = (22/7) × 20 × 7

⇒ Volume of iron = 22 × 20

⇒ Volume of iron = 440 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 440 cm3.

Additional Information

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The total CSA of a hollow cylinder is the sum of the external and internal curved surfaces: CSA = 2πRh + 2πrh = 2πh(R + r).

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The TSA includes both the CSAs and the area of the two circular rings at the ends: TSA = 2π(R + r)(h + R − r).

Volume of Solid Cylinder

If the cylinder was solid without a hole, the volume would simply be V = πr2h.

questions.question: If the areas of three adjacent faces of a rectangular box which meet in a corner are 12 cm 2 , 15 cm 2 and 20 cm 2 respectively. Then the volume of the box is
questions.questionHtml: If the areas of three adjacent faces of a rectangular box which meet in a corner are 12 cm<sup>2</sup>, 15 cm<sup>2</sup> and 20 cm<sup>2</sup> respectively. Then the volume of the box is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a rectangular box, Volume (V) = √(Area1 × Area2 × Area3)

Given Areas: A1 = 12, A2 = 15, A3 = 20

V = √(12 × 15 × 20)

V = √3600 = 60 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 60 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Area of face 1 (l × b) = 12 cm2

Area of face 2 (b × h) = 15 cm2

Area of face 3 (h × l) = 20 cm2

Formula Used:

Volume of a cuboid (V) = l × b × h

Calculations:

⇒ Let the three sides be l, b, and h.

⇒ (l × b) × (b × h) × (h × l) = 12 × 15 × 20

⇒ l2 × b2 × h2 = 3600

⇒ (l × b × h)2 = 3600

⇒ l × b × h = √3600

⇒ Volume = 60 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 60 cm3.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total surface area is given by the formula: 2(lb + bh + hl), where l, b, and h are the dimensions of the rectangular box.

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The length of the longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is √(l2 + b2 + h2).

Special Case: Cube

If l = b = h = a, then the volume is a3 and the total surface area is 6a2.

questions.question: The ratio between the length and the breadth of a rectangular park is 3 : 2. If a man cycling along the boundary of the park at the speed of 12 km/hour completes one round in 8 minutes, then the area of the park is
questions.questionHtml: The ratio between the length and the breadth of a rectangular park is 3 : 2. If a man cycling along the boundary of the park at the speed of 12 km/hour completes one round in 8 minutes, then the area of the park is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Perimeter = Speed × Time = (12000 m ÷ 60 min) × 8 min = 1600 m.

L + B = 1600 ÷ 2 = 800 m.

Ratio 3 : 2 ⇒ Total 5 parts = 800 m ⇒ 1 part = 160 m.

L = 3 × 160 = 480 m and B = 2 × 160 = 320 m.

Area = 480 × 320 = 153600 m2.

∴ The correct answer is 153600 m2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of Length (L) : Breadth (B) = 3 : 2

Cycling Speed = 12 km/h

Time taken for 1 round = 8 minutes

Formula Used:

Perimeter of Rectangle = 2 × (Length + Breadth)

Area of Rectangle = Length × Breadth

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Speed in m/min = (12 × 1000) ÷ 60 = 200 m/min

⇒ Distance (Perimeter) = 200 × 8 = 1600 m

⇒ Let Length = 3x and Breadth = 2x

⇒ 2(3x + 2x) = 1600

⇒ 10x = 1600

⇒ x = 160

⇒ Length = 3 × 160 = 480 m

⇒ Breadth = 2 × 160 = 320 m

⇒ Area = 480 × 320

⇒ Area = 153600 m2

∴ The correct answer is 153600 m2.

Additional Information

Perimeter and Area of Rectangle

The perimeter is the total boundary length 2(L + B) and area is the region enclosed L × B.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert km/h to m/min, multiply by 1000/60 or 50/3.

Diagonal of Rectangle

The length of the diagonal d is calculated using Pythagoras theorem: d = √(L2 + B2).

questions.question: If the radius of a right circular cylinder open at both the ends, is decreased by 25% and the height of the cylinder is increased by 25%. Then the curved surface area of the cylinder thus formed
questions.questionHtml: If the radius of a right circular cylinder open at both the ends, is decreased by 25% and the height of the cylinder is increased by 25%. Then the curved surface area of the cylinder thus formed
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder depends on the product of radius (r) and height (h).

Successive percentage change formula: Net Change % = a + b + (a × b)/100

Given: r decreases by 25% (a = −25) and h increases by 25% (b = +25).

Net Change = −25 + 25 + (−25 × 25)/100 = 0 − 6.25 = −6.25%.

The negative sign indicates a decrease.

∴ The correct answer is decreased by 6.25%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Change in radius (r) = −25%

Change in height (h) = +25%

Formula Used:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

Calculations:

⇒ Let original radius = r and original height = h.

⇒ Original CSA = 2 × π × r × h

⇒ New radius (r1) = r − 25% of r = 0.75r

⇒ New height (h1) = h + 25% of h = 1.25h

⇒ New CSA = 2 × π × r1 × h1

⇒ New CSA = 2 × π × (0.75r) × (1.25h)

⇒ New CSA = (0.75 × 1.25) × (2 × π × r × h)

⇒ New CSA = 0.9375 × (Original CSA)

⇒ Percentage Change = [(New CSA − Original CSA) / Original CSA] × 100

⇒ Percentage Change = (0.9375 − 1) × 100 = −0.0625 × 100 = −6.25%

⇒ The negative value signifies a decrease.

∴ The correct answer is decreased by 6.25%.

Additional Information

Volume Change in Cylinder

The volume of a cylinder is V = πr2h. If the radius changes by x% and height by y%, the net change in volume is calculated by applying the successive percentage formula twice for r and once for h.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

For a closed cylinder, TSA = 2πr(h + r). Unlike CSA, the percentage change in TSA depends on the absolute values of r and h, not just their percentage changes.

Successive Percentage Change

When a quantity depends on the product of two variables (A = x × y), and x changes by a% and y changes by b%, the net percentage change in A is always [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

questions.question: A cylindrical pencil of diameter 1.2 cm has one of its end sharpened into a conical shape of height 1.4 cm. The volume of the material removed is
questions.questionHtml: A cylindrical pencil of diameter 1.2 cm has one of its end sharpened into a conical shape of height 1.4 cm. The volume of the material removed is
questions.solution:
As we know,

Volume of the cylinder = πr2h

Volume of the cone = (1/3) πr2h

Radius of the cylinder r = 1.2/2 = 0.6 cm

Height of the cylinder h = 1.4 cm

Volume of the material removed = πr2h – (1/3) πr2h = (2/3) πr2h

⇒ (2/3) × (22/7) × 0.6 × 0.6 × 1.4

⇒ 1.056 cm3

questions.question: A rectangular park 60 m long and 40 m wide has two concrete crossroads running in the middle of the park and rest of the park has been used as a lawn. If the area of the lawn is 2109 m 2 then the width of the road is
questions.questionHtml: A rectangular park 60 m long and 40 m wide has two concrete crossroads running in the middle of the park and rest of the park has been used as a lawn. If the area of the lawn is 2109 m<sup>2</sup> then the width of the road is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two perpendicular crossroads in the middle of a rectangle, Area of Lawn = (Length − Width of road) × (Breadth − Width of road).

Let width of road be x. Then, (60 − x) × (40 − x) = 2109.

Testing Option (1): If x = 3 m → (60 − 3) × (40 − 3) = 57 × 37 = 2109 m2.

The condition is satisfied for x = 3 m.

∴ The correct answer is 3 m.

Alternate Method

Given: Length (L) = 60 m, Breadth (B) = 40 m, Area of lawn = 2109 m2.

Formula for Area of crossroads: x(L + B − x), where x is the width of the road.

⇒ Total Area of park = 60 × 40 = 2400 m2

⇒ Area of crossroads = Total Area − Area of Lawn = 2400 − 2109 = 291 m2

⇒ x(60 + 40 − x) = 291

⇒ x(100 − x) = 291

⇒ 100x − x2 = 291

⇒ x2 − 100x + 291 = 0

⇒ x2 − 97x − 3x + 291 = 0

⇒ x(x − 97) − 3(x − 97) = 0

⇒ (x − 97)(x − 3) = 0

⇒ x = 3 or x = 97. Since x cannot be greater than the park breadth (40 m), x = 3 m.

∴ The correct answer is 3 m.

Additional Information

Area of Path around a Rectangular Field (Inside)

If a path of width x is built inside a rectangle of L × B, Area of path = 2x(L + B − 2x).

Area of Path around a Rectangular Field (Outside)

If a path of width x is built outside a rectangle of L × B, Area of path = 2x(L + B + 2x).

Crossroads Calculation Shortcut

Area of two perpendicular crossroads = (L × x) + (B × x) − x2. The subtraction of x2 is necessary because the central square intersection is counted twice.

questions.question: Four circles of equal radii are described about the four corners of a square so that each touches two of the other circles. If each side of the square is 140 cm then the area of the space enclosed between the circumference of the circle is (take n = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: Four circles of equal radii are described about the four corners of a square so that each touches two of the other circles. If each side of the square is 140 cm then the area of the space enclosed between the circumference of the circle is (take n = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius of each circle (r) = Side of square ÷ 2 = 140 ÷ 2 = 70 cm.

Area of space enclosed = Area of Square − Area of 4 Quadrants

Area of 4 Quadrants = Area of 1 complete circle = πr2

Area enclosed = (140 × 140) − (22/7 × 70 × 70) = 19600 − 15400 = 4200 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 4200 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of the square (a) = 140 cm

Radius of each circle (r) = a ÷ 2 = 70 cm

Value of π = 22/7

Formula Used:

Area of square = Side2

Area of circle = π × r2

Area of four quadrants = 4 × (1/4 × πr2) = πr2

Calculations:

⇒ Area of the square = 140 × 140 = 19600 cm2

⇒ Area of the four circle sectors = (22/7) × 70 × 70

⇒ Area of the four circle sectors = 22 × 10 × 70 = 15400 cm2

⇒ Enclosed space = Area of square − Area of four sectors

⇒ Enclosed space = 19600 − 15400 = 4200 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 4200 cm2.

Additional Information

Area of a Circle Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ is given by (θ/360) × πr2. For a quadrant, θ = 90°.

Property of Tangent Circles in a Square

When four equal circles are placed at the corners of a square and touch each other, the radius of each circle is exactly half the side of the square.

General Area Formula for Enclosed Space

The area of the space enclosed between four such circles is always equal to (1 − π/4) × Side2 or approx 3/14 × Side2.

questions.question: The amount of concrete required to build a concrete cylindrical pillar whose base has a perimeter 8.8 metre and curved surface area 17.6 sq. metre, is (Take n = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: The amount of concrete required to build a concrete cylindrical pillar whose base has a perimeter 8.8 metre and curved surface area 17.6 sq. metre, is (Take n = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Radius ($r$) = Perimeter ÷ 2π = 8.8 ÷ (2 × 22/7) = 1.4 m.

Volume of Cylinder = (Curved Surface Area × Radius) ÷ 2.

Concrete required (Volume) = (17.6 × 1.4) ÷ 2 = 12.32 m3.

∴ The correct answer is 12.32 m3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Perimeter of base = 8.8 m

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 17.6 m2

π = 22/7

Formula Used:

Perimeter = 2π$r$

CSA = 2π$rh$

Volume = π$r$2$h$

Calculations:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × $r$ = 8.8

⇒ (44/7) × $r$ = 8.8

⇒ $r$ = (8.8 × 7) ÷ 44 = 0.2 × 7 = 1.4 m

⇒ CSA = 2π$rh$ = 17.6

⇒ 8.8 × $h$ = 17.6 (since 2π$r$ = 8.8)

⇒ $h$ = 17.6 ÷ 8.8 = 2 m

⇒ Volume of concrete = π$r$2$h$

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 1.4 × 1.4 × 2

⇒ Volume = 22 × 0.2 × 1.4 × 2

⇒ Volume = 4.4 × 2.8 = 12.32 m3

∴ The correct answer is 12.32 m3.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2π$r$($h$ + $r$).

Relationship between Volume and CSA

For any cylinder, the ratio of Volume to Curved Surface Area is always $r$/2.

Hollow Cylinder Volume

The volume of a hollow pipe or cylinder is given by π$h$($R$2 − $r$2), where $R$ is outer and $r$ is inner radius.

questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 9 cm, contains a liquid. This liquid is to be filled into small cylindrical bottles of diameter 3 cm and height 4 cm. Then the number of bottles necessary to empty the bowl is
questions.questionHtml: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 9 cm, contains a liquid. This liquid is to be filled into small cylindrical bottles of diameter 3 cm and height 4 cm. Then the number of bottles necessary to empty the bowl is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 54
Key Points
  • To find the number of bottles required, we need to divide the total volume of the liquid in the bowl by the volume of one cylindrical bottle.
  • The formula for the Volume of a Hemisphere is (2/3) π R3, where R is the internal radius.
  • Given: Internal radius of the bowl (R) = 9 cm.
  • Volume of the liquid in the bowl = (2/3) π (9)3 = (2/3) π (729) = 2 π (243) = 486π cm3.
  • The formula for the Volume of a Cylinder is π r2 h, where r is the radius and h is the height.
  • Given: Diameter of the bottle = 3 cm, so the radius (r) = 3/2 = 1.5 cm. The height (h) = 4 cm.
  • Volume of one cylindrical bottle = π (1.5)2 (4) = π (2.25) (4) = 9π cm3.
  • Number of bottles = (Volume of the bowl) ÷ (Volume of one bottle) = 486π ÷ 9π = 54.
  • Thus, 54 bottles are necessary to empty the bowl.
Additional Information
  • A Hemisphere is a three-dimensional geometric shape that is half of a sphere with one flat side. Its Curved Surface Area (CSA) is 2πr2 and its Total Surface Area (TSA) is 3πr2.
  • A Cylinder is a solid with two parallel circular bases. The Curved Surface Area of a cylinder is 2πrh and the Total Surface Area is 2πr(r + h).
  • When transferring liquid from one container to another, the total volume remains constant, which is the fundamental principle used to solve this problem.
  • Ensure the units for radius and height are the same (in this case, cm) before performing calculations.

questions.question: A rectangular water tank is 80 m × 40 m. Water flows into it through a pipe of 40 sq. cm at the opening at a speed of 10 km/hr. The water level will rise in the tank in half an hour is
questions.questionHtml: A rectangular water tank is 80 m × 40 m. Water flows into it through a pipe of 40 sq. cm at the opening at a speed of 10 km/hr. The water level will rise in the tank in half an hour is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rise in level = (Area of pipe × Speed of water × Time) ÷ (Base Area of tank)

Volume flow = 40/10000 m2 × 10000 m/hr × 0.5 hr = 20 m3

Rise (h) = 20 ÷ (80 × 40) = 20/3200 = 1/160 m

Rise in cm = (1/160) × 100 = 10/16 = 5/8 cm

∴ The correct answer is 5/8 cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Dimensions of tank = 80 m × 40 m

Area of pipe opening = 40 cm2

Speed of water = 10 km/hr

Time = 30 minutes = 0.5 hours

Formula Used:

Volume of water = Cross-sectional area × Velocity × Time

Rise in level = Volume ÷ Base Area of Tank

Calculations:

⇒ Area of pipe = 40 cm2 = 40 ÷ (100 × 100) m2 = 0.004 m2

⇒ Speed of water = 10 km/hr = 10,000 m/hr

⇒ Volume of water in 0.5 hours = 0.004 × 10000 × 0.5

⇒ Volume = 40 × 0.5 = 20 m3

⇒ Let the rise in water level be h meters.

⇒ Volume = Base Area × h

⇒ 20 = (80 × 40) × h

⇒ 20 = 3200 × h

⇒ h = 20 ÷ 3200 = 1/160 m

⇒ Convert h to cm: (1/160) × 100 = 100/160 = 5/8 cm

∴ The correct answer is 5/8 cm.

Additional Information

Volume Flow Rate

The volume of liquid flowing through a pipe per unit time is given by Q = A × v, where A is the cross-sectional area and v is the velocity.

Unit Conversions

1 m2 = 10,000 cm2 and 1 km = 1,000 m. Always ensure all dimensions are in the same unit before calculation.

Rise in Liquid Level

The rise in level (h) of a liquid in a container with a uniform base area is h = Volume ÷ Base Area.

questions.question: A square and a regular hexagon are drawn such that all the vertices of the square and the hexagon are on a circle of radius r cm. The ratio of the area of the square and the hexagon is
questions.questionHtml: A square and a regular hexagon are drawn such that all the vertices of the square and the hexagon are on a circle of radius r cm. The ratio of the area of the square and the hexagon is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Area of a square inscribed in a circle of radius r = 2 × r2.

Area of a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle of radius r = (3√3 / 2) × r2.

Required Ratio = 2r2 : (3√3 / 2)r2

Multiply both sides by 2 ⇒ 4 : 3√3.

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 3√3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of the circle = r cm

Square and regular hexagon are inscribed in this circle.

Case 1: Inscribed Square

For a square inscribed in a circle, the diagonal (d) of the square is equal to the diameter of the circle.

⇒ Diagonal of square (d) = 2 × r

⇒ Area of square = d2 ÷ 2

⇒ Area of square = (2r)2 ÷ 2 = 4r2 ÷ 2 = 2r2

Case 2: Inscribed Regular Hexagon

For a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle, the side length (a) of the hexagon is equal to the radius of the circle.

⇒ Side of hexagon (a) = r

⇒ Area of regular hexagon = 3√3/2 × a2

⇒ Area of regular hexagon = 3√3/2 × r2

Ratio Calculation:

⇒ Ratio = Area of square : Area of hexagon

⇒ Ratio = 2r2 : (3√3 / 2)r2

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 3√3 / 2

⇒ Ratio = 4 : 3√3

∴ The correct answer is 4 : 3√3.

Additional Information

Area of Circle

The area of the circumscribed circle is πr2. The area of any inscribed regular polygon is always less than the area of the circle.

Inscribed Equilateral Triangle

For an equilateral triangle inscribed in a circle of radius r, the side length is r√3 and the area is (3√3 / 4)r2.

General Formula for Inscribed Polygon

Area of a regular n-sided polygon inscribed in a circle of radius r = (n/2) × r2 × sin(360°/n).

questions.question: A solid cylinder has a total surface area of 231 sq. cm. If its curved surface area is 2/3 of the total surface area, then the volume of the cylinder is
questions.questionHtml: A solid cylinder has a total surface area of 231 sq. cm. If its curved surface area is 2/3 of the total surface area, then the volume of the cylinder is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of CSA to TSA is 2 : 3 ⇒ CSA / (CSA + 2 × Base Area) = 2/3.

Solving the ratio: 3 × CSA = 2 × CSA + 4 × Base Area ⇒ CSA = 4 × Base Area.

TSA = CSA + 2 × Base Area = 4 × Base Area + 2 × Base Area = 6 × Base Area.

6 × (πr2) = 231 ⇒ πr2 = 38.5 sq. cm and r = 3.5 cm.

Since CSA = 2πrh = 4πr2, we get h = 2r = 7 cm. Volume = πr2h = 38.5 × 7 = 269.5 cu.cm.

∴ The correct answer is 269.5 cu.cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Surface Area (TSA) = 231 cm2

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2/3 × TSA

Formula Used:

TSA = 2πr(r + h) = 2πrh + 2πr2

CSA = 2πrh

Volume = πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ CSA = (2/3) × 231 = 154 cm2

⇒ Total Surface Area = Curved Surface Area + 2 × Base Area

⇒ 231 = 154 + 2 × (πr2)

⇒ 2 × πr2 = 231 − 154 = 77

⇒ πr2 = 77 / 2 = 38.5 cm2

⇒ (22/7) × r2 = 38.5 ⇒ r2 = (38.5 × 7) / 22 = 12.25

⇒ r = √12.25 = 3.5 cm

⇒ CSA = 2πrh = 154

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × h = 154

⇒ 22 × h = 154 ⇒ h = 7 cm

⇒ Volume = πr2h = 38.5 × 7 = 269.5 cu.cm

∴ The correct answer is 269.5 cu.cm.

Additional Information

Surface Areas of Cylinder

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh and Total Surface Area = 2πr(r + h). The difference between TSA and CSA is always equal to twice the area of the circular base (2πr2).

Volume of Cylinder

The volume of a solid cylinder is the product of the area of its base and its height, V = πr2h.

Related Shapes

Volume of a cone with same radius and height = (1/3)πr2h. Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr3.

questions.question: The lateral surface area of a frustum of a right circular cone, if the area of its base is 16π cm 2 and the diameter of the circular upper surface is 4 cm and slant height 6 cm, will be
questions.questionHtml: The lateral surface area of a frustum of a right circular cone, if the area of its base is 16π cm2 and the diameter of the circular upper surface is 4 cm and slant height 6 cm, will be

Base radius R = √16 = 4 cm.

Upper radius r = Diameter ÷ 2 = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm.

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = π × (R + r) × l

LSA = π × (4 + 2) × 6 = 36π cm2.

Given:

Area of base = 16π cm2

Diameter of upper surface = 4 cm

Slant height (l) = 6 cm

Formula Used:

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) of frustum = π(R + r)l

Area of circular base = πR2

⇒ R2 = 16 ⇒ R = 4 cm

⇒ Upper radius (r) = Diameter ÷ 2 = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 cm

⇒ LSA = π(4 + 2) × 6

⇒ LSA = π × 6 × 6

⇒ LSA = 36π cm2

Total Surface Area of Frustum

TSA = LSA + Area of Top + Area of Base = π(R + r)l + πR2 + πr2.

Volume of Frustum

V = (1/3) × π × h × (R2 + r2 + Rr), where h is the vertical height.

Slant Height Relation

questions.question: The diameter of a sphere is twice the diameter of another sphere. The surface area of the first sphere is equal to the volume of the second sphere. The magnitude of the radius of the first sphere is
questions.questionHtml: The diameter of a sphere is twice the diameter of another sphere. The surface area of the first sphere is equal to the volume of the second sphere. The magnitude of the radius of the first sphere is

Shortcut Trick

Ratio of radii R1 : R2 = 2 : 1 (since Diameter ratio is 2 : 1)

Given: Surface Area S1 = Volume V2

⇒ 4 × π × R12 = (4/3) × π × R23

Substitute R2 = R1/2 ⇒ 4R12 = (4/3) × (R1/2)3

⇒ 4R12 = R13/6 ⇒ R1 = 24

∴ The correct answer is 24 units.

Alternate Method

Given:

Diameter of Sphere 1 (D) = 2 × Diameter of Sphere 2 (d)

Radius of Sphere 1 (R) = 2 × Radius of Sphere 2 (r) ⇒ r = R/2

Surface Area of Sphere 1 (S1) = Volume of Sphere 2 (V2)

Formula Used:

Surface Area of a Sphere = 4 × π × radius2

Volume of a Sphere = (4/3) × π × radius3

Calculations:

⇒ S1 = V2

⇒ 4 × π × R2 = (4/3) × π × r3

⇒ 4R2 = (4/3) × (R/2)3

⇒ 4R2 = (4/3) × (R3 / 8)

⇒ 4R2 = (4 × R3) / (3 × 8)

⇒ 4R2 = R3 / 6

⇒ R = 24

Additional Information

Properties of Sphere

A sphere is a perfectly round geometrical object in three-dimensional space. Its Surface Area is 4πr2 and its Volume is (4/3)πr3.

Hemisphere Formulas

For a hemisphere of radius r: Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πr2, Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3πr2, and Volume = (2/3)πr3.

Ratio of Areas and Volumes

If the ratio of radii of two spheres is a:b, then the ratio of their surface areas is a2:b2 and the ratio of their volumes is a3:b3.
